title: Vertiv introduces high power density, scalable ups system for dynamic computing environments in North America
summary: Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today launched the Vertiv™ Liebert® APM2 UPS, a modular high power density, online, three-phase uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system that introduces higher performance, expanded features and greater flexibility to today’s most dynamic computing environments.
body_text: COLUMBUS, Ohio [October 1, 2024] – Vertiv (NYSE: VRT), a global provider of critical digital infrastructure and continuity solutions, today launched the Vertiv™ Liebert® APM2 UPS , a modular high power density, online, three-phase uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system that introduces higher performance, expanded features and greater flexibility to today’s most dynamic computing environments. Liebert® APM2 is available now in North America, and will be featured in the Vertiv booth at Yotta in Las Vegas, Nevada, October 7-9. The compact and modular Liebert APM2 delivers a wide range of scalable capacities, with 10-150kVA 208V models able to parallel up to 600kVA, and 20-600kVA 480/415V models able to parallel for total system capacity up to 2.4MW. The UPS is engineered to meet the rigorous demands of diverse computing applications, including enterprise, edge, healthcare, light industrial facilities, and distributed architectures in large data centers. The Liebert APM2 can also support critical power backup to liquid cooling distribution units (CDUs) commonly deployed in high performance compute (HPC) or AI applications. The Liebert APM2 product line is highly adaptable to meet wide range of system power voltages, including 208V, 480V, and 415V, and 4 Wire, simplifying product selection to meet a variety of application needs. The modular and scalable architecture enables seamless system capacity expansion, redundancy, ease and speed of serviceability, and fault isolation to keep critical power operating. “Power protection is a concern for many data centers, especially when planning for growth,” said Ryan Motyka, global offering manager, power management, at Vertiv. “The Liebert APM2 is designed for modern IT environments and critical power applications where scalability, reliability, flexibility, efficiency and ease of deployment are prioritized.” The Vertiv™ Liebert® APM2 adopts the highly reliable and enhanced performance features of the popular Vertiv™ Liebert® EXM UPS and introduces new technologies, including Silicon Carbide (SiC) converters, to achieve even greater operating efficiencies. Additionally, the Liebert® APM2 delivers up to 20% more power module density than other market-available products with expanded capacity up to 600kVA. The Liebert APM2 also provides an integrated maintenance bypass feature up to 300kVA 480V/415V or 150kVA 208V to enable a single UPS and maintenance bypass solution. The North American models of the UPS comply with UL 1778 5th Edition and CSA 22.2 NO 107.3 for general and safety requirements. With its distributed modular architecture, Liebert APM2 power modules function independently to improve system resiliency and fault tolerance, thus improving the expected uptime to protect the critical power load. The system also offers hot swappable functionality that enables maintenance or service while under operation for core system components, including power modules, bypass module, and for select models, the new internal lithium ion or VRLA battery modules. The system can achieve efficiency rates of up to 97.5% in double conversion mode, and actively manages its hardware capacities with intelligent paralleling mode technology to operate at the highest system efficiency levels during operating load fluctuation. Additionally, Liebert APM2 includes the Dynamic Online high efficiency mode feature that delivers up to 99% efficiency without sacrificing availability of full power protection. Dynamic Online mode draws power through the bypass line and uses the inverter for a balanced output and as an active filter to provide load and network power conditioning. The Liebert APM2 offers modern and traditional flexible energy storage solutions paired with advanced battery management (BMS) system and high-capacity charging capability to achieve optimal runtime performance, battery life, and recovery from discharge. A new ultra-high density modular internal lithium battery solution is available in 10-60kVA 208V and 20-120kVA 480/415V models, further elevating the industry benchmark for UPS lithium-ion battery solutions seen on the market today. The Liebert APM2 can also be paired with optimized VRLA, lithium-ion, or nickel-zinc external battery cabinet solutions to meet a variety of applications and runtimes. First introduced in international markets in 2023, the Vertiv™ Liebert® APM2 400V CE has earned regional industry awards for product excellence and product innovation. For more information on the Liebert® APM2 or other Vertiv solutions for modern data centers, visit Vertiv.com . About Vertiv Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers’ vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extends from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, USA, Vertiv does business in more than 130 countries. For more information, and for the latest news and content from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . title: Halliburton Wins Integrated Drilling and Completions Contracts for Granmorgu Deepwater Project Offshore Suriname, Operated by Totalenergies
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Halliburton's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 13, 2026-- Halliburton (NYSE: HAL) wins major integrated well construction contracts for the GranMorgu deepwater development offshore Suriname, operated by TotalEnergies. The agreement includes drilling and completions services for a long-term program. Halliburton will deploy a fully integrated, digital and automation execution model that unites planning, engineering, and operations to improve performance, accelerate learning, and reduce total cost of ownership throughout well construction. “This award reflects the value of integrated execution, collaboration, and digital technology in complex deepwater developments,” said Franco Delano, vice president, Caribbean, Halliburton. “The GranMorgu project demonstrates how aligned teams and advanced well construction capabilities support safe, efficient delivery and maximize asset value for our customers.” Halliburton will apply integrated digital workflows, real time data and remote operations control for drilling and completions to improve well placement accuracy, and delivery assurance. These capabilities connect surface operations with subsurface execution to enhance recovery while lowering total cost of ownership for TotalEnergies. The project supports local capability development through major infrastructure investment and collaboration with local suppliers. As part of the project scope, Halliburton worked with local suppliers to upgrade its liquid mud and cement plant. The company also supported the construction of Suriname’s first state-of-the-art completions and drilling workshop, featuring advanced maintenance and repair capabilities. Halliburton will prioritize local talent acquisition and suppliers to support national economic growth. The project supports the expansion of Suriname’s offshore energy industry and establishes a benchmark through the first global alliance between Halliburton, TotalEnergies, and Noble. This integrated approach establishes a new benchmark for international unconventional fracturing. It combines electrification, automation, and advanced digital workflows to improve efficiency, consistency, and emissions-intensity reduction efforts. A common digital platform supports collaborative, phased integration of next‑generation intelligent fracturing and advanced subsurface monitoring . About Halliburton Halliburton is one of the world’s leading providers of products and services to the energy industry. Founded in 1919, we create innovative technologies, products, and services that help our customers maximize their value throughout the life cycle of an asset and advance a sustainable energy future. Visit us at www.halliburton.com ; connect with us on LinkedIn , YouTube , Instagram , and Facebook . title: What Happens if a Flock Camera Is Damaged?
summary: If a Flock LPR or video camera is damaged, agencies with the Camera Protection Plan get repair/replacement at no extra cost, no surprise bills, no paperwork.
body_text: Agencies that opt to purchase Flock’s Camera Protection Plan receive repair or replacement coverage for eligible damage. The program helps agencies quickly restore camera coverage, reducing administrative burden and avoiding unexpected repair costs. Purpose-built for public safety, Flock cameras generate investigative leads, recover stolen vehicles, help locate missing people, and provide objective evidence for investigations. The Camera Protection Plan reflects Flock's long-term commitment to supporting agencies throughout the life of their technology investment. If you’ve seen recent headlines about Flock camera vandalism, you’re probably asking the same question we’ve heard from agencies across the country: What happens if one of our cameras is damaged? Whether it’s caused by severe weather, a vehicle collision, construction, or illegal activity, such as vandalism, a damaged camera shouldn’t create another operational burden for your agency. That’s why Flock created the Camera Protection Plan, an optional annual add-on that helps agencies prepare for unexpected damage. For agencies enrolled in the Camera Protection Plan, we’ll repair or replace covered Flock LPR or video cameras at no additional cost when the damage occurs. No surprise repair bills. No uncertainty about what’s covered. Just a straightforward way to restore coverage and get your network back online. Flock’s Camera Protection Plan Is Created for the Reality of Public Safety Public safety technology doesn’t operate in a controlled environment. It sits along roadways, outside schools, at city entrances, and in parking lots. It works through storms, traffic, construction, and everything else that comes with protecting a community. After partnering with thousands of agencies across the country, we’ve learned that when a camera is damaged, replacing the hardware is rarely the hardest part. The real challenge is everything that follows: coordinating repairs, managing budgets, restoring coverage, and keeping investigations moving while your team is already responding to calls and serving the community. Agencies that choose to enroll in the Camera Protection Plan can simplify those moments by knowing exactly what comes next when damage occurs. Addressing the Questions We’re Hearing Recent incidents involving damaged Flock cameras have generated significant attention online and in the news. We’ve heard from agencies asking what those incidents mean for their own deployments. The answer is simple: we’ve planned for it. While videos shared on Reddit, X, and other platforms can make individual incidents feel widespread, they don’t reflect what we’re seeing across our network. Intentional damage remains relatively uncommon, and when it does happen, our focus is on helping agencies restore coverage as quickly as possible. We’ve also seen misinformation about why Flock cameras are being targeted. One rumor suggests they contain valuable precious metals – they don’t. Intentionally damaging public safety infrastructure can carry criminal consequences, and individuals have been arrested and prosecuted for doing so. Flock cameras are purpose-built public safety tools. Their value is in the investigative leads they generate, the stolen vehicles they help recover, the missing people they help locate, and the cases they help solve, not in the hardware itself. Illegally damaging a camera doesn’t change that mission, and it doesn’t change ours. Standing Behind the Agencies We Serve Choosing a public safety technology partner includes evaluating the hardware you install and the support, expertise, and response you can rely on when the unexpected occurs. The Camera Protection Plan reflects that commitment. For agencies with the Camera Protection Plan, covered LPR and video cameras can be repaired or replaced quickly, with no unexpected repair costs. Because protecting your camera network isn’t just about replacing equipment. It’s about ensuring the technology your officers and investigators rely on is there when they need it most. As always, we’re grateful to the agencies that trust Flock every day. We’ll continue building technology that helps you protect your communities, and standing behind it long after it’s installed.

title: The Venice Times, Vignette Collection Marks Brand Debut in Italy for IHG Hotels & Resorts
summary: IHG Hotels & Resorts (IHG), one of the world’s leading hotel companies, introduces Vignette Collection to Italy with the opening of The Venice Times Hotel, Vignette Collection, in partnership with Pacini Group. Located in one of the city’s most enviable locations, the 30-room property is now open, and is the latest addition to IHG’s first collection brand underscoring IHG's commitment to strengthening its portfolio in Italy, while leveraging Pacini Group's well-established expertise and presence in the hospitality sector.
body_text: News releases 27 July 2026 The Venice Times, Vignette Collection Marks Brand Debut in Italy for IHG Hotels & Resorts The Venice Times, Vignette collection reimagines an iconic Venetian property in partnership with Pacini Group S.p.A The Venice Times, Vignette Collection download London, UK, July 2026 - IHG Hotels & Resorts (IHG), one of the world’s leading hotel companies, introduces Vignette Collection to Italy with the opening of The Venice Times Hotel, Vignette Collection, in partnership with Pacini Group. Located in one of the city’s most enviable locations, the 30-room property is now open, and is the latest addition to IHG’s first collection brand underscoring IHG's commitment to strengthening its portfolio in Italy, while leveraging Pacini Group's well-established expertise and presence in the hospitality sector. The Venice Times, Vignette Collection invites guests to experience Venice in a new way, blending art and history in an intimate immersive flow. Hidden in the Cannaregio neighbourhood, the largest of the city’s six boroughs, the hotel is designed on a mantra where art is not decoration but part of the experience. With curated artworks displayed across the hotel intended to prompt meaningful conversation, it’s a return to the Venetian notion of culture as something to experience, discuss, and make your own. The Venice Times Hotel is a modern venetian salon where every detail invites reflection, conversation and the quiet joy of discovery. Guests can immerse themselves in art, literature and thought, discovering stories that awaken the soul and elevate the journey beyond the ordinary. The charm of the intimate property lies in every object telling a story, as art quietly accompanies life across 30 thoughtfully curated rooms. The hotel offers a tranquil base to explore Venice, located just steps away from the Casino, Ca’ d’Oro, and the Grand Canal, while the Teatro La Fenice and the Rialto Bridge are only a 15-minute walk away. For international visitors, Marco Polo airport is a 20-minute shuttle away, and Venice Santa Lucia Train Station is just 200 meters on foot. Central to Vignette Collection is the balance of individuality and belonging. A family of like-minded hotels, each property is entirely individual in its identity yet unified by the vision to offer a more authentic way to travel. Travel that is sustainably synonymous with luxury, distinction, elegance, and intrigue. This sense of individuality is encapsulated with the Manuzio Lounge, a sanctuary within the hotel perfect for taking a moment to enjoy a signature cocktail or cicchetti (a Venetian snack) in a tranquil, intimate setting, complete with a secret garden made to escape the hustle and bustle of the city streets and a rarity for such a prime location. Each Vignette Collection hotel is unique in its design yet unified by the brand’s collective vision to offer a more authentic travel experience. The brand seamlessly weaves responsibility with community and locality to bring both socially empowering and environmentally conscious experiences to its guests around the world. "The rebranding of The Venice Times as part of Vignette Collection represents another important milestone for Pacini Group and reinforces our long-term partnership with IHG Hotels & Resorts. As our second property with IHG, this project reflects the mutual trust and shared vision that continue to strengthen our collaboration over time. At Pacini Group, we believe that hospitality should create a genuine connection with its destination. With The Venice Times, we wanted to celebrate Venice's extraordinary artistic and cultural heritage, transforming it into an immersive guest experience where art, history and local identity become an integral part of every stay. We are proud to open this new chapter together with IHG and to bring Vignette Collection to Italy through a property that truly embodies the spirit of Venice." - Emidio Pacini, CEO & Owner Pacini Group. Means For Good initiatives weaved throughout all Vignette Collection properties represent each hotel’s commitment to responsibility, community engagement, and local culture with a commitment to tailoring initiatives to suit the unique character of each hotel, they partner with non-profit organizations to contribute positively to the local ecosystem. At The Venice Times, this commitment comes to life through support of the restoration of the Naval History Museum of Venice via Italy's Art Bonus programme. By contributing to the preservation of one of the city's most significant cultural landmarks, the hotel helps safeguard Venice's rich maritime heritage while reinforcing its commitment to protecting the cultural identity that makes the destination unique for future generations. Memorable Rituals – bespoke to each Vignette Collection property – connect guests with the hotel’s unique identity, locality, and cultural landscape. The Venice Times, Vignette Collection invites guest to create art in line with the history of the property, using a bespoke moveable-type kit in the lobby to make personalized postcards inspired by Aldo Manuzio, former resident and pioneering Italian Renaissance printer. Guests can further immerse themselves in Venetian culture with one off events with local artisans, such as mask-making, and photography tours. The Venice Times, Vignette Collection joins a global portfolio of over 34 Vignette Collection hotels found in 17 countries. For more information or to book a stay, visit the hotel’s website here . IHG One Rewards members can also book directly using the IHG One Rewards mobile app. For more on The Venice Times, Vignette Collection, visit the hotel’s website or follow @ihghotels , @vignettehotels and @thevenicetimes on Instagram. Ends For further information please contact: Elliot Mitchell Brand PR Manager, Europe, IHG [email protected] About IHG® IHG Hotels & Resorts (tickers: LON:IHG for Ordinary Shares; NYSE:IHG for ADRs) is a global hospitality company, with a purpose to provide True Hospitality for Good. With a family of 21 hotel brands and IHG One Rewards , one of the world's largest hotel loyalty programmes with over 160 million members, IHG has more than one million rooms across 7,000 hotels in over 100 countries, and a development pipeline of a further 2,300 properties. Luxury & Lifestyle: Six Senses , Regent , InterContinental , Vignette Collection , Kimpton , Hotel Indigo Premium: Noted Collection , voco , Ruby , HUALUXE , Crowne Plaza , EVEN Essentials: Holiday Inn Express , Holiday Inn Hotels & Resorts , Garner , avid Suites: Atwell Suites , Staybridge Suites , Holiday Inn Club Vacations , Candlewood Suites Exclusive Partners: Iberostar Beachfront Resorts InterContinental Hotels Group PLC is the Group's holding company and is incorporated and registered in England and Wales. Approximately 400,000 people work across IHG's hotels and corporate offices globally. Visit us online for more about our hotels and reservations and IHG One Rewards . To download the IHG One Rewards app, visit the Apple App or Google Play stores. For our latest news, visit our Newsroom and follow us on LinkedIn . About Vignette Collection Vignette Collection is IHG’s first collection brand and newest addition to its luxury and lifestyle portfolio. It represents a fast-growing family of unique properties each offering one-of-a-kind stays in destinations to remember. Collectively different and proudly independent, Vignette Collection hotels share the vision to harness travel’s ability to benefit local people and places weaving responsibility, community, and locality together. Since its launch in 2021, the brand has surpassed the halfway point in its initial aim to reach 100 hotels in the first 10 years. Today, the collection encompasses 34 hotels in 17 countries globally with a further 45 properties in the pipeline. Vignette Collection was launched to offer owners of world-class independent hotels the ability to benefit from IHG’s powerful enterprise offering and global scale whilst retaining their hotel’s unique character, style, and name. For more information, visit www.vignettecollectionhotels.com Pacini Group For over 20 years, Pacini Group has been dedicated to the art of hospitality as a Hospitality Developer, creating outstanding projects and memorable guest experiences through a multidisciplinary approach and a distinctive, forward-thinking vision. Pacini Group is synonymous with luxury, warm hospitality, and highly personalized service. The Group’s portfolio includes its Hospitality Division, structured across three business lines. Prestige features five luxury hospitality properties: The Pantheon Iconic Rome Hotel – Autograph Collection and The Goethe Hotel in Rome, together with the newly opened Palazzo Rota in Venice and The Venice Times – Vignette Collection. In the midscale segment, the portfolio includes Garner Hotel Rome Aurelia and Unica Suites & Apartments, offering luxury suites and apartments in the heart of Rome. Completing the portfolio is the Group’s Food & Beverage Division, which comprises three distinctive dining concepts: the Michelin-starred Idylio by Apreda, Divinity Restaurant & Lounge Bar at The Pantheon Iconic Rome Hotel, and Affinity Kitchen & Alchemy, the restaurant and lounge bar at The Goethe Hotel in Rome. Research, passion, creativity, expertise, and continuous innovation are the core values that drive the company, led by Emidio Pacini. title: Best Apps That Combine Calendar + To-Do List (2026)
summary: Compare the five best apps that combine a calendar and to-do list in 2026, with honest recommendations for manual planning, automation, and fast capture.
body_text: Summary Akiflow is the best overall calendar and to-do list app for professionals who need to collect work from several tools and turn it into a realistic schedule. Sunsama is best for a guided planning ritual, while Motion is best for people who want software to rebuild the schedule automatically. Morgen suits complex calendar setups, and Todoist remains the strongest lightweight choice when fast task capture matters more than a full planning command center. What are the best apps that combine calendar and to do list in 2026? The five best apps that combine a calendar and to-do list in 2026 are Akiflow, Sunsama, Motion, Morgen, and Todoist. Akiflow is our best overall pick because it puts tasks from multiple work tools beside the calendars that determine when those tasks can actually happen, without forcing the user to surrender control of the schedule. This ranking was checked on July 27, 2026. It is deliberately short. A product earned a place only if it handles both sides of the job: remembering work and making time for it. We looked at capture speed, calendar visibility, time blocking, integrations, rescheduling, mobile and desktop access, and the amount of daily maintenance each system creates. The products are not interchangeable. Akiflow is a consolidation tool for a busy work stack. Sunsama is a guided daily planner. Motion is an automatic scheduler with a broader work platform around it. Morgen is strongest when several calendars and task sources need one planning layer. Todoist is still primarily a task manager, but its calendar layout now makes it a credible lighter option. The five best calendar and to-do list apps at a glance Akiflow Best for: Consolidating work and planning it on a calendar Planning model: User controlled with AI assistance Current price signal: $19 yearly or $34 monthly Main limitation: Too expensive for a simple checklist Sunsama Best for: A guided and realistic daily planning ritual Planning model: Deliberate manual planning Current price signal: $17 yearly or $22 monthly Main limitation: The ritual can feel slow Motion Best for: Automatically rebuilding a busy schedule Planning model: High automation Current price signal: $19 yearly for Pro AI Main limitation: Less direct control over changes Morgen Best for: Planning across several calendar accounts Planning model: Calendar first with AI support Current price signal: $15 yearly or $30 monthly Main limitation: Less focused on universal task intake Todoist Best for: Fast capture with a lighter calendar layer Planning model: Task first manual planning Current price signal: Free plan and paid upgrades Main limitation: Not a full planning command center 1. Akiflow is the best overall choice Akiflow is the best choice for people whose tasks arrive from more places than one list can comfortably hold. Its Universal Inbox collects work from connected tools, while the calendar, time blocking, quick capture, keyboard shortcuts, and daily planning ritual turn that incoming work into a plan the user can see and adjust. The distinction is important. A normal calendar integration can display due dates, but it does not necessarily help someone decide what deserves Tuesday at 10:00. In Akiflow, a task from email, Slack, Notion, Todoist, or a project tool can enter the inbox, keep a link to its source, and then be scheduled beside fixed meetings. That makes the calendar a decision surface rather than a second database. Akiflow also leaves the final scheduling judgment with the user. Aki can help create tasks, organize work, and handle planning commands, but the experience is not built around silently rebuilding the entire day. That balance is particularly useful for founders, operators, consultants, and managers whose priorities change for reasons an algorithm may not understand. The related calendar and task integration guide explains the workflow in more depth. The drawback is price. The current Akiflow plan is $34 per month or $19 per month billed yearly after a seven-day trial. That is difficult to justify for a simple personal checklist. It makes more sense when fragmented intake, calendar negotiation, and repeated context switching are already costing meaningful time each week. Akiflow puts the task list and weekly calendar in one workspace, letting users move incoming work into visible time blocks while keeping control of the plan. 2. Sunsama is best for guided daily planning Sunsama is the best choice for someone who wants planning to be a deliberate daily ritual. Its guided flow asks the user to review unfinished work, import tasks and meetings, estimate durations, check the planned workload, defer excess commitments, and then decide which tasks should be timeboxed on the calendar. That sequence is more than interface polish. Sunsama compares planned task time with a workload threshold and shows whether the day is likely to run past the preferred shutdown time. Tasks can come from its backlog or connected systems such as Asana, Jira, Todoist, Gmail, and calendars. The result is a calmer plan built around capacity rather than an optimistic list. The tradeoff is pace. People who enjoy the ritual often find it grounding; people who already know what they need to schedule may find the extra steps slow. Sunsama also asks the user to make most prioritization decisions rather than automatically resolving the calendar. Its current Pro plan is $17 per month billed yearly or $22 billed monthly, with a 14-day trial. 3. Motion is best for automatic scheduling Motion is the strongest pick when the buyer wants the software to decide when flexible work should happen. Tasks carry priorities, deadlines, and durations; Motion places them around meetings and can replan the calendar as conditions change. That is a different promise from a manual time-blocking tool, and for the right user it removes real planning labor. Motion now extends well beyond a personal calendar. Its Pro AI plan includes projects and tasks, calendar and meetings, docs, notes, integrations, an AI task planner, and apps across desktop and mobile. The breadth is useful for a small team that wants project execution and scheduling in the same system, rather than a planner sitting on top of several existing tools. The limitation follows from the strength: the schedule can feel like the software's opinion of the day. Users who want to protect a particular block for strategic or personal reasons may prefer a planner where changes are more explicit. Motion's official pricing page lists Pro AI at $19 per seat per month on annual billing and Business AI at $29. 4. Morgen is best for multiple calendars Morgen is the best fit when calendar fragmentation is the central problem. It brings Google, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail, and other calendar accounts into one view, connects task systems such as Todoist, Notion, Linear, ClickUp, and Google Tasks, and supports time blocking with its AI Planner across desktop, mobile, browser, and Linux. This makes Morgen attractive to consultants, agency owners, and anyone managing separate personal, client, and company calendars. The planning layer can show conflicts across those accounts, while scheduling links and a booking page reduce the need for a separate meeting tool. It provides more calendar breadth than a task manager with one calendar view bolted on. Morgen is less compelling when the main pain is rapid capture from messages and work apps. It connects many task sources, but Akiflow offers a more pronounced inbox-to-calendar workflow. Morgen's individual plan is $30 billed monthly or $15 per month billed yearly. That pricing makes it a strong value when cross-calendar planning is the actual requirement. 5. Todoist is best for lightweight capture Todoist is the best lightweight option for people who primarily need an excellent task manager and only occasionally plan work on a calendar. Quick Add, natural-language dates, recurring tasks, priorities, filters, and broad platform support make capture unusually fast. The Pro calendar layout adds enough visual planning for many personal and small-team workflows. In calendar layout, a user can drag an all-day task into a time slot and resize it to set a duration. Todoist also syncs with Google Calendar and supports reminders and deadlines on paid plans. This is a meaningful improvement over a list-only setup, especially for someone who wants one familiar app rather than a dedicated daily planning system. Todoist still behaves like a task manager first. Its task duration documentation notes that start dates are not supported, and it does not provide the same universal intake and calendar review workflow as Akiflow. Choose it when simplicity is an advantage, not when work is already scattered across several operational tools. How should you choose between these five apps? Choose by identifying which decision is currently expensive. Pick Akiflow when work arrives from several tools and you want to decide the schedule quickly. Pick Sunsama when overcommitment and an inconsistent planning habit are the problems. Pick Motion when choosing times is the burden you want to delegate. Pick Morgen when multiple calendars create the confusion. Pick Todoist when capture is the main need. Then test the product with a normal, imperfect week. Connect the calendars that really control your availability, bring in ten active tasks, schedule three important pieces of work, and allow a meeting to move. The useful question is not whether the first plan looks clean. It is whether the app makes the second plan obvious after the first one breaks. Pay attention to maintenance. Count how many times work must be copied, how often a date and a calendar block disagree, and whether unfinished tasks are easy to recover. A premium planner should reduce those decisions, not decorate them. Readers who want to compare planning styles more broadly can use this daily planning app guide as the next step. Frequently asked questions What is the best app that combines a calendar and to-do list? Akiflow is the best overall choice for professionals who need tasks, calendars, integrations, and time blocking in one place. Sunsama is better for a guided ritual, Motion for automatic scheduling, Morgen for multiple calendars, and Todoist for a lighter task-first workflow. Is Akiflow better than Sunsama? Akiflow is better when fast capture, connected task sources, keyboard control, and direct calendar execution matter most. Sunsama is better when the user wants a slower guided planning process that checks workload and encourages deliberate shutdown. Both are manual-first planners, but they create very different daily rhythms. Is Motion better than Akiflow for scheduling? Motion is better if automatic rescheduling is the main reason for buying the app. Akiflow is better if the user wants to collect work from several tools, see it beside the calendar, and retain control over what moves. The choice is between delegated scheduling and faster human-directed planning. Can Todoist replace a dedicated daily planner? Todoist can replace a dedicated planner when task capture, due dates, reminders, and occasional calendar blocking cover the workflow. It becomes less complete when the user needs one inbox for several work tools, a structured planning ritual, or frequent recovery from meeting-heavy days.
